newsitem.title: UK: European forex trading grinds to a Christmas halt.
newsitem.headline: European forex trading grinds to a Christmas halt.

text.p: The dollar was steady in Europe as the European market ground to a halt on Christmas Eve with some centres, including Germany, already closed for the break.
Traders in London were looking for a short day's trading and the market here will effectively finish business soon after midsession, dealers said.
At 0800 GMT the dollar was at 1.5538/43 and 114.33/43, little changed from Monday's late European levels of 1.5550/60 and 114.01/11.
There are no U.S. economic data today but U.K. trade data are due at 0930 GMT.
Japan's index of leading indicators stood at 83.3 in October, above the so-called boom-or-bust level of 50 for the second consecutive month.
A figure above 50 is generally taken as suggesting that the economy will expand in the coming months.

The mark was steady on the crosses with mark/Paris showing little reaction to news that the French October trade surplus was 16.94 billion francs against the 10.6 billion forecast and revised 9.7 billion in September.
Mark/Paris was at 3.3750/55 against 3.3735 late Monday in Europe.
Sterling was a little firmer when compared with Monday's close with U.K. trade data due at 0930 GMT.

The non-EU trade deficit is seen at around 635 million sterling in November after 424 million in October while the October global shortfall is seen at around the same level after an 899 deficit in September.
Sterling was at 2.6079/90 marks against Monday's 2.6010/20 with cable at $1.6768/78 against a previous $1.6708/13.
